key_insight: CRC-HGD introduces a multi-magnification histopathology dataset for training AI models to grade colorectal cancer across three WHO differentiation levels.
clinical_relevance: A standardized labeled image dataset can support development and benchmarking of automated tools that may help pathology workflows assess colorectal cancer grade more consistently.
method: Collected 1,914 H&E-stained microscopy images from 214 colorectal adenocarcinoma patients.
Annotated specimens into WHO grades I, II, and III (well-, moderately-, and poorly-differentiated).
Provided four magnification levels per specimen: 4x, 10x, 20x, and 40x.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports dataset size, patient counts, grade distribution, and multi-scale image availability, but does not present model performance results.
watch_item: Grade imbalance and single-center collection may limit generalizability, so external validation is needed before real-world use.
paper_title: CRC-HGD: A Histopathological Image Dataset for Grading Colorectal Cancer
